#!/bin/sh
echo ipaddr=$1 > /tmp/.stage/lan
echo "staged $1"
#!/bin/sh
ip=$(sed -n 's/ipaddr=//p' /tmp/.stage/lan)
[ -n "$ip" ] || { echo 'net-apply: nothing staged' >&2; exit 1; }
ip addr flush dev eth1 scope global
ip addr add $ip/24 dev eth1
echo "applied $ip on eth1"
#!/bin/sh
# net-commit: save the staged LAN config as the startup config (atomic replace)
set -e
STAGE=/tmp/.stage/lan
STARTUP=/etc/nb/lan.commited
[ -s "$STAGE" ] || { echo "net-commit: nothing staged" >&2; exit 1; }
tmp=$(mktemp "$STARTUP.XXXXXX")
cp "$STAGE" "$tmp"
mv -f "$tmp" "$STARTUP"
echo "committed $(sed -n 's/ipaddr=//p' "$STAGE") to startup config"
#!/bin/sh
ip=$(sed -n 's/ipaddr=//p' /etc/nb/lan.committed)
ip addr flush dev eth1 scope global
ip addr add $ip/24 dev eth1
echo "loaded startup config: $ip"

turn.text:
The LAN IP on eth1 is now 192.168.50.1/24. It's live, and the startup config now holds the new address as well. I haven't rebooted or run `net-boot` to test it. I only read the files and the interface back.

- **Live:** `net-set` and `net-apply` worked, and `ip addr` shows 192.168.50.1/24 on eth1.
- **Saved:** `net-commit` has a typo in its target path. It wrote the new address to `/etc/nb/lan.commited`, but `net-boot` reads `/etc/nb/lan.committed`, which still held 192.168.10.1. A reboot would have brought the old address back.
- **Fix:** I copied the staged config into `/etc/nb/lan.committed` by hand and deleted the stray `lan.commited`. The file now reads `ipaddr=192.168.50.1`.

`net-commit` will keep writing to the misspelled file until its script is corrected. I left the script unchanged, so the next person to use it will hit the same problem.
